title: TRY/EXCEPT/ELSE Flow
description: Use ELSE block to run code only when no error occurs in TRY block.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Sometimes you want to do something ONLY if the operation succeeded—like logging success or proceeding to next step. That's what ELSE is for."
story.context: ELSE block runs only when TRY succeeds (no error). This creates clean success/failure paths without nested IF statements.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! Navigation check succeeded, so ELSE block ran and logged 'Navigation online'. If it had failed, EXCEPT would have run instead. Clean branching logic."

instructions: - (Do NOT use Fail - let it succeed)
- Log 'Navigation online - proceeding to route calculation'
hints: ELSE comes after EXCEPT, before END
ELSE runs ONLY if TRY succeeded (no error)
If error occurs: TRY → EXCEPT (skip ELSE)
If no error: TRY → ELSE (skip EXCEPT)

*** Test Cases ***
Navigation System Check
    ${nav_status}=    Set Variable    checking
    TRY
        Log    Testing navigation system...
        ${nav_status}=    Set Variable    online
        Log    Navigation test passed
    EXCEPT    AS    ${error}
        Log    Navigation failed: ${error}
        ${nav_status}=    Set Variable    offline
    ELSE
        Log    Navigation online - proceeding to route calculation
    END
    Log    Final status: ${nav_status}

theory.title: Exercise 3.2.3: TRY/EXCEPT/ELSE
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "You've learned to handle errors with EXCEPT. But what about handling SUCCESS? That's where ELSE comes in—code that runs ONLY when TRY succeeds."

TRY/EXCEPT/ELSE Flow Control

ELSE block runs only when TRY completes without error:

TRY
    # Code that might fail
    Operation
EXCEPT
    # Runs if error occurs
    Log    Error path
ELSE
    # Runs if NO error occurs
    Log    Success path
END

Execution Flow:

  • If TRY succeeds: TRY → ELSE (skip EXCEPT)
  • If TRY fails: TRY → EXCEPT (skip ELSE)
  • Code after END always runs

Example: Success vs Failure Paths

${status}=    Set Variable    unknown
TRY
    Log    Checking sensor...
    # Fail    Sensor offline  # Uncomment to test error path
    ${status}=    Set Variable    ok
EXCEPT    AS    ${err}
    Log    Sensor check failed: ${err}
    ${status}=    Set Variable    error
ELSE
    Log    Sensor check passed - calibrating...
END
Log    Sensor status: ${status}

Without Fail (success path): Logs "Checking sensor...", "Sensor check passed - calibrating...", "Sensor status: ok"

With Fail (error path): Logs "Checking sensor...", "Sensor check failed: Sensor offline", "Sensor status: error"

⚠️ TRY/EXCEPT/ELSE Rules

  • ELSE must come AFTER EXCEPT
  • ELSE is optional (can have just TRY/EXCEPT)
  • ELSE never runs if error occurred
  • Use ELSE for success-specific logic (logging, next steps)
  • Cleaner than nested IF statements checking for errors
